source: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj. Excerpts are abridged; 'terms' are search words for retrieval, 'anchors' are what the judge expects to find in a note before it accepts the citation, 'remedy' is the default recommendation the offline drafter uses.

articles.title: Storage limitation
articles.text: Personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed.
articles.remedy: System owner to configure automated deletion or anonymisation against the retention schedule and evidence the first run before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Lawfulness of processing
articles.text: Processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that at least one of the following applies: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task or legitimate interests (abridged).
articles.remedy: Process owner to document the legal basis for each affected purpose and stop any processing without one before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Conditions for consent
articles.text: Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented. The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time. It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent.
articles.remedy: Marketing lead to keep per-person consent records and make withdrawal as easy as giving consent before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Processing of special categories of personal data
articles.text: Processing of personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, or trade union membership, and the processing of genetic data, biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation shall be prohibited.
articles.remedy: DPO to confirm a valid exception for the special-category data and restrict access to it before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Time limit for answering data subject requests
articles.text: The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 15 to 22 to the data subject without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request. That period may be extended by two further months where necessary.
articles.remedy: Privacy team to track each data subject request against the one-month deadline and send extension notices in time, evidenced before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Right of access by the data subject
articles.text: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed, and, where that is the case, access to the personal data.
articles.remedy: Privacy team to set up a documented process that gives data subjects a copy of their data, tested before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Right to erasure
articles.text: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her without undue delay and the controller shall have the obligation to erase personal data without undue delay where one of the grounds applies.
articles.remedy: System owners to propagate erasure to every copy (backups, warehouses, processors) or suppress restored records, and evidence it before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Data protection by default
articles.text: The controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures for ensuring that, by default, only personal data which are necessary for each specific purpose of the processing are processed.
articles.remedy: Product owner to switch defaults to the least data needed and record the decision before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Processor contract
articles.text: Processing by a processor shall be governed by a contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law, that is binding on the processor with regard to the controller and that sets out the subject-matter and duration of the processing, the nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data and categories of data subjects and the obligations and rights of the controller.
articles.remedy: Procurement to sign a data processing agreement covering the Article 28 terms with the processor before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Records of processing activities
articles.text: Each controller and, where applicable, the controller's representative, shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility.
articles.remedy: DPO to complete the missing entries in the record of processing activities and set a review cycle before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Security of processing
articles.text: The controller and the processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of those measures (abridged).
articles.remedy: IT security to implement and evidence the missing technical control (logging, access control or encryption) for the affected system before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
articles.text: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority. Where the notification is not made within 72 hours, it shall be accompanied by reasons for the delay.
articles.remedy: DPO to fix the breach procedure so the authority is notified within 72 hours, with reasons for any delay documented, before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Data protection impact assessment
articles.text: Where a type of processing in particular using new technologies is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data.
articles.remedy: DPO to complete a DPIA for the processing, apply the resulting measures and consult the supervisory authority if high risk remains, before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Designation of the data protection officer
articles.text: The controller and the processor shall designate a data protection officer where their core activities require regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale, or consist of processing on a large scale of special categories of data (abridged).
articles.remedy: Management to designate a data protection officer and publish the contact details before the follow-up audit.

articles.title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
articles.text: In the absence of an adequacy decision, a controller or processor may transfer personal data to a third country or an international organisation only if the controller or processor has provided appropriate safeguards, and on condition that enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies for data subjects are available.
articles.remedy: Legal to put appropriate safeguards (standard contractual clauses plus a transfer impact assessment) in place for the transfer, or stop it, before the follow-up audit.
